bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable sudoers parser, the `<EXPECTPATH>` lexer rule materializes `CHROOT=` path tokens as heap strings and immediately registers them in `parser_leak_list` under `LEAK_PTR`. The staged PoC's line 11 is `b'user\xda\tALL = CHROOT=/v CHROOT=/var/ww/binlts\truncwd=~'`; among the witness's `CHROOT` values, only the first `/v` token matches AddressSanitizer's reported 3-byte region. The first `options chrootspec` reduction stores that tracked `/v` pointer in `$$.runchroot`. When the second `CHROOT=` on the same options chain is reduced, vulnerable `plugins/sudoers/gram.y:799-800` frees the old `$$.runchroot` and replaces it with the later `/var/ww/binlts` string but never removes the old pointer from `parser_leak_list`. After `sudoersparse()` returns, the fuzz target's cleanup call `init_parser(NULL, false, true)` re-enters `parser_leak_init()`, which takes its already-initialized arm and drains the leak list. `parser_leak_free()` eventually reaches the stale `LEAK_PTR` entry for `/v` and frees it a second time. The fix expresses the missing obligation by calling `parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runcwd)` and `parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runchroot)` before those frees.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled path that later becomes the stale freed pointer. In `<EXPECTPATH>` state entered by `CHROOT`, the lexer reads the witness token `/v` and builds `sudoerslval.string` from those bytes.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 635-byte sudoers text file. Its line 11 is `b'user\xda\tALL = CHROOT=/v CHROOT=/var/ww/binlts\truncwd=~'`, so the first path token after `CHROOT=` is exactly `/v`. That gives `fill(..., sudoersleng)` a 2-byte token and ultimately yields the 3-byte `"/v\0"` allocation reported by AddressSanitizer.

sink.description: ASan sink. While draining `parser_leak_list`, `parser_leak_free()` reaches a stale `LEAK_PTR` entry that still points to the already-freed `/v` string and calls `free()` on it again.
sink.note: The saved crash stack is `free -> parser_leak_free -> parser_leak_init -> init_parser`, and ASan reports that the crashing region is the same 3-byte allocation previously freed from `sudoersparse()` at `gram.y:799`.

root_cause.description: The `options chrootspec` reduction frees the previous `runchroot` string before removing its `LEAK_PTR` bookkeeping entry, so the global leak list keeps a dangling pointer to freed storage.
root_cause.note: The patch adds `parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runcwd);` and `parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runchroot);` immediately before these frees. The saved previous-free stack also points to this exact `gram.y:799` site.

tainted_value_origin.code: dst = olen ? realloc(sudoerslval.string, olen + len + 1) : malloc(len + 1);
tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete heap allocation later freed twice. For the witness token `/v`, `fill_txt()` allocates a 3-byte string buffer that persists in parser state and the leak list.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: AddressSanitizer reports a 3-byte region `[0x6020000005b0,0x6020000005b3)`. Among the witness's `CHROOT` path tokens, only line 11's literal `/v` produces `len + 1 == 3`, matching that allocation exactly.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved allocation stack is `malloc -> fill_txt -> sudoerslex`.

parser_admitted.description: The saved ASan previous-free stack proves the witness reaches the second `options chrootspec` reduction at `gram.y:799`, so the parser definitely enters the vulnerable repeated-`CHROOT=` path before cleanup.

fine_trace.note: Source. In `<EXPECTPATH>` state for the first `CHROOT=` on PoC line 11, the lexer copies the attacker token `/v` into a heap-backed `sudoerslval.string`. Because that token is 2 bytes long, the underlying allocation is the 3-byte `"/v\0"` region later reported by ASan.
The reproducing fuzz build has leak tracking enabled, so the lexer immediately records that `/v` buffer in global `parser_leak_list` as a `LEAK_PTR` entry for later parser cleanup.

On the first `options chrootspec` reduction for that line, the inherited `$$.runchroot` is still NULL from `init_options()`, so `free(NULL)` is harmless and `options.runchroot` becomes the same tracked `/v` pointer from step 2. This creates the alias that the later replacement frees.

Root cause and first free. The same witness line later reaches a second `CHROOT=` (`/var/ww/binlts`) on the same options chain, so this reduction frees the old `/v` string from step 3 and replaces `$$.runchroot` with the new `$2` pointer. Because no `parser_leak_remove(LEAK_PTR, $$.runchroot)` happens first, `parser_leak_list` still retains a stale entry for the just-freed `/v` buffer.

After `sudoersparse()` returns, the fuzz target calls `init_parser(NULL, false, true)`. Because the earlier `init_parser("sudoers", false, true)` already set the static `initialized` flag, `parser_leak_init()` takes this cleanup arm and starts freeing every still-tracked parser object, including the stale `/v` entry left by step 4.

Sink. While draining `parser_leak_list`, `parser_leak_free()` eventually reaches the stale `LEAK_PTR` entry for `/v` and frees that same 3-byte buffer again. This matches the saved ASan crash stack `free -> parser_leak_free -> parser_leak_init -> init_parser` and the previous-free location at `sudoersparse` line 799.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack is `malloc -> fill_txt -> sudoerslex`, and it reports a 3-byte region. That size matches the PoC line 11 token `/v\0` exactly.

free_context.note: ASan's previous-free stack points to the `options chrootspec` reduction at `gram.y:799`. Among the staged PoC's `CHROOT` values, only line 11's first `/v` token has the reported 3-byte allocation size.

format.name: sudoers-policy-text
format.contract: The staged PoC is a sudoers text witness whose line 11 contains `CHROOT=/v CHROOT=/var/ww/binlts\truncwd=~`, so the parser materializes a first 2-byte `CHROOT` path `/v`, stores it in `options.runchroot`, then replaces and frees that same pointer on a later `CHROOT=` in the same options chain while its `LEAK_PTR` entry still remains in `parser_leak_list`. The fuzz target's subsequent `init_parser(NULL, false, true)` cleanup call then triggers the second free.
